newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W. AUSTRALIA CANOLA POOL PRICE RISES, BARLEY FALLS.
newsitem.headline: W. AUSTRALIA CANOLA POOL PRICE RISES, BARLEY FALLS.

text.p: The Grain Pool of Western Australia has increased its 1997/98 pool indicators for canola but reduced prices for barley and lupins, it said on Wednesday.
The canola indicator price had been increased by A$2.00 a tonne to a range of A$340.00-A$350.00 a tonne. This followed concerns over the Canadian canola crop, it said.

Improved growing conditions on Australia's east coast last week, with good rain across much of eastern Australia following earlier indications of a dry season, had caused indicators for barley and lupins to be reduced, it said.
Pool prices had been reduced by A$5.00 a tonne to A$190.00-A$200.00 for malting barley and by A$2.00 to A$150.00-A$155.00 for feed barley, the Grain Pool said.
The pool price for lupins had been reduced by A$2.00 a tonne to A$188.00-A$193.00, it said.

Grain Pool chief executive officer Kevin Swan said the indicators were likely to fluctuate more regularly as the growing season progressed toward harvest because markets were influenced by weather and growing conditions.
"Just a week ago barley prices lifted because the east coast was so dry. Substantial rain last week means a more positive production outlook," he said in the Grain Pool's statement.
Lupin prices had been influenced by an estimated improvement in production of protein feed crops, he said.
